purpose: Register a known prescribed-field approximation as an unresolved, scoped scientific question with a follow-up and a provisional use decision.
known_at_implementation: The source introduced in 79ffd569001ee238469f3e32bb432e6bb2fa63f0 already declares no line trapping, continuum attenuation or thermal balance. This records a known approximation, not prior knowledge of its quantitative error.

source.finding: Line and continuum occupations are computed once and shared by every layer. Observer transfer does not feed radiation back into populations.

literature.finding: The authors use a PHOENIX incident stellar spectrum and iterate Cloudy temperature/ionization structure with the wind. Their complete Cloudy input files are not available in the reviewed archive.
Cloudy distinguishes the incident boundary field, its attenuation through matter, and diffuse radiation. This documents the distinction, not the exact options of the paper's c23.01 run.

retained_diagnostic.calculation_scope: Optical depths of prescribed-field populations, not a converged radiation-population solution.
retained_diagnostic.column_convention: Radial outward column from each layer midpoint to 3 Rp: sum full exterior cells plus half the current cell. Total columns span 1 to 3 Rp.
retained_diagnostic.line_convention: Static thermal/full-lifetime line centers. H-alpha uses the observer common NIST center and three branches; Ly-alpha uses the resolved 2p->1s atomic transition.

interpretation: These samples cannot justify treating the relevant Lyman channels as optically thin.
The optical depths do not determine the self-consistent mean intensity or the H-alpha model error.
The diagnostic was performed after the observer implementation; it strengthens an already known concern.
No coupled radiation/population-to-observer comparison or physical model-error budget has yet been reviewed.

next_comparison.vary: Prescribed local field versus internally transported radiation coupled to statistical equilibrium.
controls: Optically thin limit with matched boundary mean intensity
Spatial/frequency/atom refinement sufficient to separate numerical errors from closure effects
outputs: H-alpha spectra with the same observation operator
next_comparison.acceptance: Declare a physical error budget and parameter domain before comparison; the existing 0.1-sigma numerical refinement criterion is not automatically that budget.
next_comparison.completion: Archive the controlled comparison and its own numerical Claim/Assessment, then review the implications for radiation-closure adequacy without inferring physical validation from numerical agreement alone. Preserve this unknown review and record remaining discrepancies with a further action or scoped use Decision; implementation or solver convergence alone is insufficient.
